sentences.text: Surge operations begin when queue age, simultaneous high-priority calls, or staffed unit availability crosses thresholds approved by regional policy.
Regional Dispatch Center monitors these indicators continuously and declares the applicable surge level when a threshold is met.
Computer Aided Dispatch Console displays the current surge level and the operational constraints reported by field and facility staff.
Triage Supervisor validates the declaration and confirms that call prioritization remains consistent with clinical protocols.
Shift Commander assigns coordination responsibilities and reviews whether normal coverage can be maintained during the surge.
Regional Medical Director provides clinical direction when demand exceeds routine triage guidance or requires a regional protocol adjustment.
Hospital Liaison Desk uses the Pediatric Acuity Note to convey pediatric monitoring and destination considerations to receiving staff.
Pediatric calls with concerning airway, breathing, circulation, or mental status findings receive prompt clinical escalation under approved protocols.
Call Taker Mara obtains the age, weight when available, and caregiver observations needed to support pediatric triage.
Paramedic Crew reassesses pediatric patients during transport and reports material changes to the receiving facility.
Kestrel shall confirm that facility capacity and pediatric service limitations are communicated to dispatch before a destination is finalized.
Riverside Trauma Center advises Hospital Liaison Desk when trauma intake conditions may affect the suitability of an otherwise appropriate destination.
Emergency Department staff acknowledge destination changes through the established coordination channel and identify any immediate access restrictions.
Hospital Liaison Desk records facility responses in the regional coordination record and keeps dispatch informed of unresolved constraints.
Mutual aid is requested when local staffed units cannot meet the declared response objectives or when a specialized resource is unavailable.
Regional Radio Network carries mutual-aid requests, acceptance confirmations, and operational updates using the agreed regional call signs.
Copperfield shall approve any temporary triage override and document its rationale before the override is applied.
Ambulance Coordination Platform tracks accepted mutual-aid assignments separately from locally staffed resources to preserve an accurate coverage view.
Ambulance Unit 417 may be reassigned only after dispatch confirms that its current patient-care and transport obligations permit the change.
Fleet Maintenance Cell reports a vehicle restriction promptly so dispatch does not count an unavailable unit toward operational coverage.
Triage Supervisor reviews the audit memo before closing a suspected duplicate incident.
Data Quality Officer reviews unresolved record discrepancies through the established quality process without delaying active patient care.
North Gate Status Board provides a current view of access conditions that may affect ambulance approach or handover timing.
South Gate Status Board provides the equivalent access view for routes and entry points on the southern side of the region.
After surge conditions ease, Shift Commander confirms that outstanding assignments, destination constraints, and staffing gaps have been handed over to the next operational period.
